title: Almanac chapter three, with two sections that have no subject here

projectIdentity.summary: A printed almanac for smallholders in the eastern valleys, written by one author and edited by one editor. The house words are fixed: a 'panel' is one facing pair of pages, a 'stub' is a paragraph the editor has marked for expansion, and 'the run' is the print run of eight thousand copies scheduled for the autumn.

decisions.summary: Chapter order was locked to the growing season rather than to crop type, because a reader consults the almanac by the month in front of them and never by taxonomy. The frontispiece was locked as a woodcut rather than a photograph, because the run is one colour and a halftone reproduces badly at this paper weight.

workflow.summary: The author drafts a panel, the editor marks stubs, the author expands every stub before the panel is called done. Nothing goes to the typesetter with an open stub in it.

architecture.summary: This project is a printed book written by one author. There is no system, no service and no process model for this section to describe, and the physical structure of the book is already covered under decisions as the chapter order.

constraints.summary: The run is eight thousand copies at one colour, and the chapter must fit sixteen panels exactly, because the binder folds in signatures of thirty-two pages.

rejectedPaths.summary: A month-by-month index was drafted and abandoned: it duplicated the chapter order it was meant to help a reader navigate, and it cost two panels the chapter does not have.

executiveSummary.summary: Chapter three of a printed almanac, at capture eleven of sixteen panels drafted with four stubs open. The single most important next thing is expanding the stub on overwintering, which the editor marked twice.

currentTask.summary: At capture, expanding the four open stubs in panels seven through eleven. Done means no open stub remains in the chapter and the editor has read it once end to end.
